short_description: Consumer-facing lifestyle trait that reports a cautious panel-relative signal for walking-for-pleasure frequency tendency within the current local reference panel.
summary_note: Usable consumer-facing movement trait describing a cautious inherited signal related to how often someone tends to walk for pleasure relative to the current local reference panel.
what_it_measures: A panel-relative polygenic signal associated with frequency of walking for pleasure, calibrated within the current local empirical reference panel.
interpretation_template: This is a cautious panel-relative movement signal, not a direct readout of how often you currently go walking for pleasure. {interpretation}
caution_text: Use as a cautious panel-relative signal only. No imputation or ancestry-adjusted normalization is used, and the output should not be treated as a direct readout of current leisure walking habits, fitness, or health status.
limitations: Percentiles and z-scores are relative to the local reference panel, not to a population-wide benchmark.
Real-world leisure walking depends strongly on neighbourhood, safety, time, climate, age, health, and personal preferences.
This trait should not be used as a judgment of discipline, lifestyle quality, or cardiovascular fitness.
confidence_note: Confidence reflects overlap and reference robustness under the no-imputation raw-array workflow, not certainty about the real-world trait.
reference_note: Percentiles and z-scores are calibrated against a local empirical reference artifact built from raw-array files in this project; they are panel-relative, not population-wide.
